Decision-Grade Multi-Objective Benchmarking and Emulation of Controller Placement in Software-Defined Networks

Principal Investigator: Thabang Mhlokoma (Honours B.Sc. Computer Science) • Supervisor: Prof. Mudali
Department of Computer Science
Faculty of Science, Agriculture & Engineering
"Driving Sustainable Futures Through Interdisciplinary Research & Digital Innovation"

1 Background & Motivation

SDN Architecture

Software-Defined Networking (SDN) decouples control logic from physical forwarding hardware. In multi-site WANs, optimizing the Controller Placement Problem (CPP) is an NP-hard facility location challenge balancing propagation latency, fault tolerance, and computational cost.

The Methodological Gap: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is frequently advocated for CPP. However, existing studies evaluate models on single-metric latency under isolated conditions, ignoring computational energy costs, training runtimes, and real-world OpenFlow validation.

2 Research Questions

Objectives
RQ1 (Performance & Latency): How do DRL algorithms (PyTorch DQN) compare against classical heuristics (K-Means, Greedy K-Center) in minimizing propagation latency L(P) and maximizing N−1 reliability?
RQ2 (Complexity Tax ω): What computational overhead (s/episode) is incurred by AI models across varying topology scales (N = 20, 50)?
RQ3 (Hardware-in-the-Loop Emulation): Do algorithmic rankings translate to real OpenFlow control Round Trip Times (RTT) in Mininet?

3 5 Placement Paradigms & Pipeline

Methodology
1. Random Baseline O(1)
Stochastic uniform node selection baseline.
2. Greedy K-Center O(k·N)
Gonzalez 2-approx minimax radius heuristic.
3. K-Means Medoids O(I·k·N)
Graph geodesic shortest-path partitioning.
4. Genetic Algorithm O(G·P)
Combinatorial evolutionary crossover search.
5. PyTorch Deep Q-Network (DQN) DRL Model
Adaptive neural placement (64×64 MLP), γ = 0.99, α = 0.001, replay buffer 10⁴, ε-greedy decay.

4 3-Axis Multi-Objective Pareto Space

Trade-Off Analysis
Fig. 2. Joint 3-Axis Pareto space: Latency L(P) (ms) vs N−1 Reliability Reachavg (%) vs Compute Time ω (s).

The non-dominated Pareto frontier proves that K-Means Clustering and Greedy K-Center achieve the optimal trade-off boundary—delivering minimal latency with near-zero compute overhead (ω < 0.005 s).

5 DQN Training & Policy Dynamics

1,000 Episodes
Fig. 3. 1,000-episode DQN reward trajectory on Internet2 (N = 34, k = 3), converging within 20 episodes.

DQN converged rapidly to a mean reward of 13.199 (total runtime: 21.26 s, ω = 0.0213 s/episode). However, it incurs a 4,000× computational tax over heuristic clustering without achieving lower propagation latency.

6 Mininet OpenFlow Emulation

Emulated Validation

Hardware-in-the-loop control RTT was measured in real-time across virtual Open vSwitch networks on Internet2 WAN (N = 34, k = 3):

Algorithm Paradigm Control RTT Compute ω N−1 Rel. Pareto Rank
K-Means Clustering TOP 2.852 ms 0.003 s 100% Rank 1
Greedy K-Center 3.104 ms 0.002 s 100% Rank 2
PyTorch DQN 2.914 ms 21.26 s 100% Rank 3
Genetic Algorithm (GA) 3.180 ms 0.450 s 100% Rank 4
Random Baseline 4.820 ms 0.0001 s 85.2% Rank 5
Statistical Significance: Factorial ANOVA confirms significant algorithmic effect (F(4, 55) = 89.4, p < 0.001). Post-hoc Tukey HSD proves K-Means significantly outperforms GA and Random baselines.

7 Sustainable Decision Framework

Operator Guide
✓ Static WANs (N ≤ 50)

Deploy K-Means / Greedy K-Center: Sub-5ms compute overhead, zero GPU requirement, minimal energy consumption, and provable latency bounds.

⚡ Dynamic / Volatile WANs

Deploy PyTorch DRL / DQN: Strictly justified when facing real-time topology churn, high-frequency link degradation, or multi-tenant traffic shifts.

8 Conclusions & Recommendations

Key Takeaways

• Decision Efficiency: For static WANs, classical clustering delivers optimal decision quality without neural training overhead.

• Sustainable Digital Innovation: Eliminating unnecessary AI compute aligns directly with green networking paradigms by avoiding computational complexity taxes.

• Practical Recommendation: Adopt a tiered placement architecture—use deterministic heuristics as the primary operational backbone, triggering DRL adaptation only during severe network churn.
